The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has accused President Bola Tinubu of insensitivity to the plight of Nigerians following his insistence that the country must move on from fuel subsidy removal. The Council said the President’s position showed a lack of empathy for millions of Nigerians grappling with rising food prices, transportation costs, poverty and the worsening cost of living. Tinubu had, at a rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, urged Nigerians to forget about fuel subsidy, declaring that the policy belonged to the past. But reacting to the President’s remarks during an interaction with youths in Lokoja, Kogi State, ahead of the ADC presidential campaign rally scheduled for Tuesday, the ADC-PCC Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, said the President was disconnected from the economic realities facing ordinary Nigerians. Ologbondiyan accused Tinubu of being more concerned about his presidential status than addressing the hardship confronting citizens. “The President appears more interested in being addressed as Mr President than in tackling the crushing realities confronting the people. He has demonstrated little or no concern for the suffering of ordinary Nigerians. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The ADC-PCC questioned how the consequences of a policy that continues to shape the daily experiences of millions of Nigerians could be dismissed as a thing of the past. It argued that the removal of fuel subsidy was implemented without adequate preparation, effective social safety nets, or sufficient measures to cushion its impact on vulnerable households. According to the Council, the policy has contributed to soaring transportation costs, rising food prices, difficulties confronting small businesses and the further impoverishment of millions of households. “To ask Nigerians to forget a policy whose consequences they confront every waking moment is not only insensitive; it is an insult to their intelligence and a mockery of their suffering,” Ologbondiyan added. Ex-NDC spokesman Abdulsalami defects to Atiku’s ADC ADC crisis: Gombe mocks Atiku as feud deepens Single-digit: Test of dropping inflation The opposition campaign council maintained that responsible leadership required the willingness to listen to citizens, acknowledge policy shortcomings and make necessary adjustments to ease their economic difficulties. It also accused the Tinubu administration of defending its economic policies despite the hardship it has imposed on Nigerians. Beyond the economic situation, the ADC-PCC raised concerns over what it described as the weakening and manipulation of critical democratic institutions, including the judiciary, security agencies, anti-corruption bodies and financial institutions, allegedly in pursuit of the President’s second-term ambition. It warned that public institutions established to protect democracy and serve the national interest must not be subordinated to the political ambitions of any individual. “Nigeria cannot afford a second term built on the ruins of its democratic institutions and the continued impoverishment of its citizens,” the Council declared. The ADC-PCC said the country’s economic difficulties were not inevitable but could be addressed through better policy choices, adequate planning and leadership that prioritised citizens’ welfare. It consequently presented the ADC presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, as the alternative capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening democratic institutions and improving living conditions. The Council promised that an Atiku-led administration would pursue economic policies backed by proper planning, effective social protection programmes and a people-centred approach to governance. It urged Nigerians to use lawful and constitutional means to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, insisting that the next general election would provide an opportunity to change the country’s direction. deserve a government that feels their pain, understands their struggles and takes deliberate steps to ease their burden, not one that dismisses their suffering or asks them to forget the circumstances that have made life increasingly unbearable,” it added.
